Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

This is the no-Bookshelf ablation: no cross-domain fish-control research shelf
is provided. Base controller proposals only on the task contract, current and
inherited guidance, sampled solver results, inherited optimizer logs, and
current rollout evidence. Do not search for or reconstruct the omitted shelf
from neighboring configurations or repository history.

I’m using the `read-wake-visual-signals-first` skill because this task changes a multi-wake target policy. I’ll first read its full instructions and `README.md`, then inspect the current rollout evidence before touching the solver.

The contract confirms the candidate must stay non-empty, visual diagnosis must precede any policy edit, and formal CFD is out of scope. I’m now mapping the available sampled results, inherited optimizer notes, and current candidate so I can compare the strongest finite run with the most diagnostic failure.

The sampled evidence has one longer, physically informative seed failure (`82b…`, 50.13 released time, transient 8.61L minimum, then lower-boundary exit) and three much earlier right-boundary exits near 16.3–16.7. Per the skill, I’m inspecting the shared held-fish prewarm first, then the released sheets—especially the longer seed and the early-exit controller closest to the current parent.

The visual sheets agree with the metrics: the seed self-propels aggressively but turns almost vertically and never enters the useful target wake; all three feedback variants barely bend their path, drift down-right with the developed flow, and exit before one shedding cycle. I’m now tracing each policy and inherited note to identify which mechanism caused that shared early-exit topology and which bounded change is genuinely new.

The inherited results sharpen the failure boundary: merely slowing/desaturating the gait did not help—three target-aware variants were almost passively advected out the downstream boundary—while the only opposite-sign bearing controller was unbounded and became unstable after 1.01 time units, so it cannot validate the steering sign. The visual-first skill now requires me to record this diagnosis and the bounded intermediate-drive hypothesis in the candidate notes before editing the policy.

The candidate architecture is fixed: correct the body-frame bearing sign, raise propulsion from the under-driven sampled band, retain energy regulation, and impose a 20-rad/time² smooth ceiling to stay well below the hard envelope. I’m applying that single solver candidate and a durable negative lesson that distinguishes under-driven advection from the inherited unbounded instability.

The single candidate, provenance notes, and reusable lesson are now updated. I’m invoking the prescribed static checker sequence: semantic guidance change first, then the lightweight Julia contract/schema probe, then the editable-boundary guard. I will not run CFD.

The semantic checker found a rendered-workspace metadata defect: the same assigned parent is marked “copied to guidance” twice. Both markers name `optimizer_6a2fe42ff255`; I’m removing only the duplicate marker so the assignment remains unchanged, then rerunning the required check.

The semantic check passes. The Julia probe is blocked only by the login shell’s PATH (`julia: command not found`); the inherited run found a workspace/runtime installation, so I’m locating that executable without changing the candidate, then I’ll rerun the exact probe and continue to the boundary guard.
